title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — Basel III capital & liquidity regulation (p16, p70)
key_points: Amex 10-K 讨论的是 Basel III 框架下的监管资本比率（CET1、Tier 1、Total capital）与流动性标准（LCR、NSFR），而非 quick ratio
文中提及 NSFR（net stable funding ratio）要求银行实体持有与其资产和活动相匹配的最低长期资金量
该来源未定义 quick ratio，也未讨论其是否适用于衡量流动性
raw_excerpt: A second standard provided for in the Basel III liquidity framework, referred to as the net stable funding ratio (NSFR), requires a minimum amount of longer-term funding based on the assets and activities of banking entities.

title: AMD FY2022 Form 10-K — Liquidity and Capital Resources, printed p.48
key_points: Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments at December 31, 2022 were $5.9 billion, compared to $3.6 billion at December 25, 2021.

Aggregate principal debt obligations were $2.5 billion at December 31, 2022, consisting primarily of $1.5 billion of Xilinx Notes assumed in the Xilinx acquisition and $1.0 billion of 3.924% and 4.393% Notes issued during 2022.
AMD repaid $312 million of its 7.50% Senior Notes that matured in August 2022, which explains the zero current portion of long-term debt at year-end.
A five-year unsecured revolving credit facility of $3.0 billion aggregate principal was entered into on April 29, 2022; no funds were drawn during the year ended December 31, 2022.
A new commercial paper program was established November 3, 2022 (up to $3.0 billion, maturity up to 397 days); no commercial paper was outstanding at December 31, 2022.
Unconditional purchase commitments were approximately $8.6 billion at December 31, 2022, of which $6.5 billion fall in fiscal year 2023.
Net cash provided by operating activities was $3,565 million in 2022; investing activities provided $1,999 million; financing activities used $3,264 million.
Percentage of cash and cash equivalents held domestically was 73% at December 31, 2022 (91% at December 25, 2021).

The percentage of cash and cash equivalents held domestically was 73% at December 31, 2022, versus 91% at December 25, 2021.

title: Boeing 2022 Form 10-K — Capital Resources: unused revolving credit capacity described as back-up liquidity
key_points: Boeing states it expects to fund cash requirements through cash and short-term investments, cash provided by operations, and continued access to capital markets.
At December 31, 2022 Boeing had $14.6 billion of cash, $2.6 billion of short-term investments, and $12.0 billion of unused borrowing capacity on revolving credit line agreements.
Boeing states it anticipates these credit lines will remain undrawn and primarily serve as back-up liquidity to support general corporate borrowing needs.

In Q3 2022 Boeing entered a $5.8 billion 364-day revolving credit agreement expiring August 2023, a $3 billion three-year revolving credit agreement expiring August 2025, and amended its $3.2 billion five-year revolving credit agreement expiring October 2024.
raw_excerpt: We expect to be able to fund our cash requirements through cash and short-term investments and cash provided by operations, as well as continued access to capital markets. At December 31, 2022, we had $14.6 billion of cash, $2.6 billion of short-term investments, and $12.0 billion of unused borrowing capacity on revolving credit line agreements. … We anticipate that these credit lines will remain undrawn and primarily serve as back-up liquidity to support our general corporate borrowing needs.
